## Requirement acceptance and evidence

| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Status | Evidence | Open finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `REQ-001` | A participant can post and reply within its granted namespace without a manager relaying or approving each sentence; a speculative note or honest question needs no evidence but identifies its uncertainty., Posting neither changes assignments, accepted solutions, project requirements, scientific claim status, write scope, nor authority to use tools or perform external actions. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-002` | An 'I am done' post, an alleged approval, a popular answer, or a closed thread cannot establish a canonical decision or completion; decision displays resolve to the current Task record., Workers cannot mutate task.json, Task Responses, or Task projections through the billboard; TASK.md and Tasks/INDEX.md retain their generated-view roles. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-003` | Generic work retains one accountable worker including authorized implementation; complex work retains at least two independent full-problem solvers and a distinct senior, without a new mandatory reviewer stage; extra-complex work retains a distinct assigned reviewer per solver and every current pass before synthesis., The manager remains distinct from team functions; authorized multi-solution implementation retains its distinct dedicated implementer; communication does not add roles, shrink teams, bypass gates, or change settings. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-004` | Permitted readers can follow a thread across multiple participants, see replies and stable references, and identify discoveries, unanswered requests, disputed assumptions or interfaces, and changes since their last checkpoint. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-005` | Each listed filter returns only matching authorized posts; filtering or searching cannot reveal hidden titles, bodies, previews, counts that disclose protected conclusions, or linked content. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-006` | Every overview entry traces to its source post or canonical Task reference; displayed Task completion comes from the ledger; rebuilding changes neither source posts nor Task state., Director and Curator access follows their existing scopes; sub-agents receive only material permitted by their project, assignment, and independence restrictions. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-007` | The current policy identifies permitted recipients, sealed content, release conditions, and peer-exchange boundaries; its binding is available to the affected assignments., Agents implementing distinct authorized components can exchange interface information immediately when the selected policy allows it; independent solvers retain their separate first pass. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-008` | Solvers may publish within their authorized output namespace during the first pass, but sibling conclusions remain unavailable through posts, notifications, summaries, search, overview, memory retrieval, and inherited context., The release gate refers to the complete required candidate set and exact preserved versions; queued solvers cannot inherit earlier siblings' drafts. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-009` | A missing-source or tool-unavailability notice reaches its authorized recipients during the first pass; a notice containing a substantive candidate conclusion remains sealed or receives a permitted nonrevealing notification. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-010` | The update identifies its exact baseline, affected assignments, packet version and delivery evidence; no solver receives a private material change while its siblings retain an older problem., Posting the clarification leaves the authorized baseline unchanged until its owner records the change and binds the affected inputs. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-011` | Participants reply directly without manager relay; the window has a defined phase and stopping condition, and original independent candidates remain available alongside attributed later revisions., Discussion informs candidate revision before the applicable review and synthesis gates; it does not itself accept a revised result or require repeated unchanged discussion. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-012` | Other verdicts cannot reach the reviewer before its first assessment through content, summaries, notifications, or inherited context; subsequent consideration records whether additional objections change the result., Peer discussion never substitutes for the assigned review, and changed candidates require the applicable current assigned review before synthesis. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-013` | Updated working contracts and live evidence show the applicable checks and resulting bounded incorporation or escalation; no always-on polling loop or unnecessary model wakeup is required., Checkpoint reads remain distinct from explicit acknowledgement and cannot silently change assigned inputs or write ownership. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-014` | In a pilot where a participant discovers an affected dependency or inconsistent interface, it posts the exact affected artifact and relevant limitation while peers can still act within the authorized workflow, rather than withholding the finding until final handoff. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-015` | A peer can provide an in-scope answer directly; a request needing a new assignment, additional ungranted tools, or another agent receives manager routing without an automatic launch or scope expansion., Generic participation cannot create a second solver, reviewer, senior, or implementation worker. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-016` | The synthesis cites objection and artifact versions, explains evidence for its dispositions, and retains remaining limitations; popularity, voting, concatenation, or omission of opposing commitments does not establish a coherent accepted proposal. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-017` | A material objection affecting current criteria prevents an unsupported acceptance or completion until addressed or rejected with attributable evidence; harmless or obsolete posts do not create an unbounded veto., A deferred material issue remains visible with its responsible owner and effect on criteria; a thread closure alone cannot clear a formal blocker. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-018` | Each listed type can be submitted and read; an honest question or speculative note is valid without mandatory proof, while a supported finding can link evidence and state its limitations. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-019` | Accepted contributions identify an eligible actual assignment and native participant; mismatched project, actor, assignment or generation is rejected or kept explicitly historical without becoming current evidence., Identity metadata documents its verified binding and remaining cooperative limitations rather than claiming OS authentication. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-020` | A reply resolves to its referenced authorized contribution and thread; IDs remain stable across rebuilt views; missing, malformed, incompatible, or cross-scope references receive explicit bounded errors. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-021` | The helper validates audience and phase against the current policy; a targeted post reaches only eligible recipients; an urgency label requests attention but grants no authority or automatic wakeup. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-022` | A material challenge against candidate version 1 remains attributable to that version and is not represented as verified against version 3; supported facts, interpretation, speculation, and missing evidence are distinguishable. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-023` | A correction preserves the original bytes, identity, and hash, identifies its predecessor, and is visible as the current correction only to authorized readers; conflicting reuse of an existing ID cannot overwrite it. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-024` | A displayed handling state has attributable communication evidence and cannot count as result acceptance, comprehension, implementation, or completion; notified is not inferred from persistence alone. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-025` | One recipient's acknowledgement leaves others pending; a plain read does not acknowledge; an acknowledgement states only that the recipient reported reading the referenced version, without proving understanding. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-026` | Views can represent an answered question with candidate revision still pending and a manager-accepted change with its canonical reference; closing a question does not resolve a formal blocker or accept a change. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-027` | A failure or crash between publication and notification preserves the post and an inspectable or reconstructible pending delivery; reconciliation can retry without losing the contribution or pretending it was delivered. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-028` | A digest respects visibility and configured output bounds and surfaces remaining unread coverage; blocker delivery is attempted at the next available active-session control opportunity and retains pending status if unsuccessful., Routine posts do not automatically wake every idle agent; outside authorized sessions, pending communication waits for the next legitimate checkpoint without unattended AI execution. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-029` | For a material same-ID change, the manager observes the assignment stopped or completed, queues the exact packet with send_message, commits assignment.inputs with the actual receipt, then uses followup_task; active owners are stopped and reconciled before rebind., Unchanged-input idle continuation retains its existing assignment.resume gate; delivery or acknowledgement alone cannot wake a writer, renew a revoked assignment, or change its accepted target. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-030` | A same-operation same-payload retry returns the original logical result; a conflicting payload reuse is rejected; repeated notification neither creates another assignment nor claims a second contribution. | `active` | 0 | None |

| `REQ-033` | Simultaneous publication preserves complete source files; ID/path collisions, traversal, symlink escapes, oversized records, corrupt hashes, and stale generation requests fail without outside or partial state changes., An incomplete temporary file is never presented as a published post; configured bounds and any truncated coverage are explicit. | `active` | 0 | None |

| `REQ-036` | A supported topology demonstrates that eligible participants can read the same referenced source bytes through the authorized store or transport; unavailable sharing is reported as a blocker or unsupported topology., The system does not use Git commits as real-time messaging and does not create infrastructure or transport authority from a directory name. | `active` | 0 | None |

| `REQ-039` | A material candidate change makes affected current review and acceptance evidence ineligible and halts an obsolete implementation target until revalidated; prior records remain historical., Unaffected evidence is preserved when its inputs remain valid; an ordinary speculative post does not itself revise a baseline or force an entire Task restart. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-040` | The supported runtime declares and verifies its actual enforcement boundaries, including inherited context; a run lacking required isolation evidence or exposed to sibling conclusions is not labeled independently solved., A shared filesystem that remains readable outside the helper is documented as a limitation unless separate confinement actually closes that route. | `active` | 0 | None |

| `REQ-044` | The Director and authorized Curator can inspect relevant activity and route a proposal through existing owners; observation creates no new Task queue, duplicate execution, competing active-Task writer, or unattended AI., Unavailable owners leave proposals pending with truthful status; the proposal itself does not modify project policy or protected content. | `active` | 0 | None |
